column.text: Bitcoin's $76k support is the level that decides the next move, and the tape leans bearish into it. Momentum is stretched but not broken: BTC RSI sits at 35.21, oversold, while the MACD histogram stays negative. Price is stabilizing, but sellers have not stepped away. Money is leaving spot. BTC ETFs shed $398.6M on Monday 2 Nov, taking the seven-day net to −$739.1M. ETH lost $139.8M on the same day, with a seven-day net of −$567.0M. SOL was flat on Tuesday 3 Nov at +$0.0M, though its seven-day net is −$71.5M, so the outflow is broad. Derivatives tell a different story. Hyperliquid's top-30 desks are heavily net short, BTC −$623M and ETH −$505M, so a bounce could force covering. Sentiment reads Fear at 34. A falling tape is not a short signal here. Our shorts have mostly been entered after the drop and stopped on the bounce, so the default is no short. Any short needs a mechanism you can point to in the printed blocks, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20-day MA, or negative funding. Counter-trend longs are for high-conviction reversals at clear support with a catalyst, never reflexive dip-buys. Dollar liquidity is flat, so trade the structure. Headlines add noise. Binance's $6.3B exploit still coincided with $1.822B in 24-hour net inflows, and Democratic sweep odds of 87%–95% are pressuring Nasdaq 100 futures, down about 1.5%. Watch $76k: a clean break confirms downside, while a reclaim with rising open interest changes the picture.
